Baba.description: Topshe's father and friend of Dhiru Kaka who plans the family holiday.

Feluda.description: An intelligent and eccentric private detective and cousin to Topshe, known for his sharp deductive skills.

Dhiru Kaka.description: A lawyer living in Lucknow and childhood friend of Topshe's father who hosts the family; his bedroom was the site of the ring's disappearance.

Dr Srivastava.description: Dr Srivastava is an osteopath in Lucknow, recipient of a valuable ring, described as nervous and a genuine Lucknowwalla. He is the owner of the stolen ring and tries to reassure Dhiru Kaka after its loss.

Jagmohan.description: Dhiru Kaka's bearer, helps around the house.

Din Dayal Singh.description: The driver who picks up the family from the station.

Pyarelal Seth.description: A wealthy Gujarati businessman from Lucknow who gifted a valuable ring to Dr Srivastava.

Mahabir.description: Pyarelal Seth's son, cured by Dr Srivastava.

Bonobihari Babu.description: A retired businessman and descendant of Bengal zamindars who owns a private zoo.

Mr Jhunjhunwalla.description: Dr Srivastava's next-door neighbour, described as very rich.

Mr Billimoria.description: Another neighbour of Dr Srivastava, also wealthy.

Bhudeb Mitra.description: A barrister whose house was recently burgled.

Lucknow.description: A historic city in northern India, known for its architecture and culture.

Haridwar.description: A holy city in Uttarakhand, India, famous for its temples and the Ganges river.

Laxmanjhoola.description: A suspension bridge and pilgrimage site near Rishikesh, Uttarakhand.

Darjeeling.description: A hill station in West Bengal, India, known for tea and scenic views.

Puri.description: A coastal city in Odisha, India, famous for its beaches and the Jagannath Temple.

Bhoolbhulaia.description: A maze inside the Burra Imambara in Lucknow, built by the nawabs.

Burra Imambara.description: A grand historical monument in Lucknow, famous for its maze.

Residency.description: A historical site in Lucknow, central to the British forces during the Mutiny.

Mutiny.description: Refers to the Indian Rebellion of 1857 against British rule.

Tagore.description: Rabindranath Tagore, renowned Bengali poet and Nobel laureate.

Secunder Bagh.description: An area in Lucknow, site of Dhiru Kaka's house and historical significance.

Fiat.description: An Italian car brand, used here to describe Dr Srivastava's vehicle.

Aurangzeb.description: A Mughal emperor, son of Shah Jahan, referenced as the ring's original owner.

Shah Jahan.description: A Mughal emperor, father of Aurangzeb, famous for building the Taj Mahal.

Samarkand.description: A historic city in Uzbekistan, referenced in the story of Aurangzeb.

Agra.description: A city in Uttar Pradesh, India, famous for the Taj Mahal, where Pyarelal bought the ring.

Jahannan Khan.description: A historical figure mentioned as a possible owner of the ring.

Madhya Pradesh.description: A central Indian state, referenced as a place where dacoits are common.

Bengal.description: A region in eastern India, referenced as Bonobihari Babu's ancestral home.

Europe.description: A continent, referenced as a destination for exported animals.

America.description: Refers to the United States, mentioned as a destination for animals.

Australia.description: A country and continent, also mentioned as a destination for animals.

Calcutta.description: Now Kolkata, a major city in eastern India, referenced as Pyarelal's former residence and compared to Lucknow.

Kaka.description: A term meaning uncle in Hindi and Bengali, used for older male relatives or friends.

Imambara.description: A Shia Muslim shrine or congregation hall, often architecturally significant.

nawab.description: Nawab is the title for Muslim rulers or noblemen in India, especially in Lucknow, and is used both as a vocabulary term and as a proper noun.

tonga.description: A horse-drawn carriage commonly used for transport in Indian cities.

ekka.description: A single-horse carriage, smaller than a tonga.

namaskaar.description: A respectful Indian greeting, involving folded hands.

Lucknowwalla.description: A colloquial term for someone native to Lucknow.

daku.description: Hindi word for bandit or robber.

dacoit.description: A term for a member of a band of armed robbers in India.

Seth.description: A title used for wealthy businessmen, especially in northern India.

typhoid.description: An infectious disease common in India, referenced as the cause of death for Pyarelal's son.

zamindar.description: A landowner, historically a hereditary title in Bengal and other parts of India.

Charminar.description: Charminar is a popular Indian cigarette brand, also referred to in the plural as Charminars.

paan.description: A betel leaf preparation chewed for its stimulant effects, common in India.

Kaiser Bagh.description: A locality in Lucknow known for its Mughal-era architecture; the name humorously combines Urdu and German.

Badshah Manzil.description: A historical building in Lucknow, pointed out by the tongawalla during the ride.

Chandiwali Barradari.description: Another notable Mughal-era structure in Lucknow, mentioned during the sightseeing.

Lakhu Phatak.description: A place or landmark in Lucknow, referenced by the tongawalla.

Rumi Darwaza.description: A famous gateway in Lucknow, known for its impressive Mughal architecture.

Machchli Bhawan.description: A building in Lucknow, near which the Burra Imambara is located.

Laxmanavati.description: The ancient name for Lucknow, referencing its legendary founder Laxman.

Chowk Bazar.description: A well-known market area in Lucknow.

Delhi.description: The capital city of India, known for its historical monuments and political significance.

Bombay.description: The former name of Mumbai, a major city in India and the center of the Bollywood film industry.

Diwali.description: A major Hindu festival known as the Festival of Lights, celebrated across India.

attar.description: A fragrant essential oil, often used as perfume in South Asia.

Ganesh Guha.description: Caretaker of Bonobihari Babu's zoo, known for his strength and fearlessness.

Badshah.description: Bonobihari Babu’s massive black hound, serves as the real bodyguard of the house.

Mughal.description: Relating to the Mughal Empire, known for its distinctive art and architecture.

Munger.description: A city in Bihar, India, known for its historical significance.

Africa.description: The continent from which some of the exotic animals originate.

Anglo-Indian.description: A term referring to people of mixed Indian and British ancestry or relating to British India.

Alipore.description: A locality in Kolkata, famous for the Alipore Zoo.

Ram Lila.description: A traditional dramatic folk re-enactment of the life of Lord Rama, performed during Dussehra.

Dussehra.description: A major Hindu festival celebrating the victory of good over evil.

Ramayana.description: An ancient Indian epic narrating the life of Lord Rama.

Ram.description: The hero of the Ramayana, regarded as an incarnation of Vishnu.

Lakshman.description: Brother of Ram in the Ramayana, known for his loyalty.

Ravan.description: The antagonist in the Ramayana, a demon king defeated by Ram.

veranda.description: A roofed platform along the outside of a house, typically level with the ground floor.

laddoo.description: A round Indian sweet made from flour, sugar, and ghee.

Sandile ka laddoo.description: A specific variety of laddoo, a sweet from Lucknow.

gulabi reori.description: A pink-colored Indian sweet, often made with sesame seeds and sugar, popular in northern India.

bhoona pera.description: A type of sweet from Lucknow, made by roasting and reducing milk.

sadhubaba.description: Sadhu is a Hindu holy man or ascetic, while sadhubaba is a term for a holy man or ascetic in India.

bearer.description: A domestic servant or attendant, especially in Indian English usage.

Inspector Gargari.description: A police inspector known to Dhiru Kaka.

Frazer Road.description: A street where Dhiru Kaka lives.

Dupling Road.description: A road connected to Frazer Road in Lucknow.

Ramakrishna Mission.description: A well-known spiritual and philanthropic organization in India.

Doon Express.description: A train that runs to and from Dehra Dun.

Imperial Express.description: A fictional or possibly real train mentioned humorously by Feluda.

Dehra Dun.description: A city in northern India, home to Doon School.

Doon School.description: A prestigious boarding school in Dehra Dun, India.

Life.description: A magazine that Feluda is seen reading.

Mars.description: The planet Mars, mentioned in conversation.

moon.description: Earth's natural satellite, mentioned in conversation.

Park Road.description: A road in Lucknow mentioned as a landmark.

Istishan.description: The Urdu word for 'station', referring to the railway station.

Hindi.description: The most widely spoken language in India, referenced in the context of a film.

Daku Mansoor.description: The title of a Hindi film being advertised in the story.

muffler.description: A scarf worn around the neck for warmth.

babu.description: Babu is a respectful term for a man, often used in northern India for gentlemen or educated men. It is also used as a term of respect in India.

meetha.description: Hindi word for 'sweet', used here to describe a type of paan.

masala.description: A mixture of spices used in Indian cuisine and also in paan.

paise.description: A subunit of the Indian rupee.

Thakur.description: A title used in northern India, often for a respected or noble person.

carrom.description: A popular tabletop game in South Asia, similar to billiards but played with disks.

Denticare.description: A brand of toothpowder mentioned as a disguise for something else.

Banaras.description: Also known as Varanasi, a city in India famed for its paan and spiritual significance.

Henry Lawrence.description: The British Commander-in-Chief during the Siege of Lucknow in the Mutiny, killed during the conflict.

Sir Colin Campbell.description: A British general who led reinforcements to relieve the besieged Residency during the Mutiny.

Allahabad.description: A city in northern India, mentioned as the place where Dr Srivastava's father worked.

Standard.description: Refers to the Standard car, a brand of automobile popular in India during the mid-20th century.

sannyasi.description: A sannyasi is a Hindu ascetic or holy man who has renounced worldly possessions; the plural form is sannyasis.

attaché case.description: A small, flat suitcase used for carrying documents, often associated with professionals.

Godrej almirah.description: A Godrej almirah is a steel cupboard or wardrobe manufactured by the Indian company Godrej, commonly used for secure storage. The term 'almirah' refers more generally to a cupboard or wardrobe, while 'Godrej' is the brand.

goonda.description: A Hindi slang term for a thug or gangster.

Tapesh.description: Feluda’s younger cousin and the narrator of the story who assists in investigations.

Mr Malkani.description: Owner of Malkani & Co., an antique and curio shop in Hazratganj.

Mr Pestonji.description: A local customer of Malkani & Co., known for purchasing valuable items like Persian carpets.

Pritam Singh.description: Bearer in Mahabir's household, previously served Pyarelal Seth in Calcutta, and witnessed events surrounding Seth's death.

Dr Graham.description: Pyarelal Seth's regular doctor, absent during the critical events, attending a conference in Allahabad.

Hazratganj.description: A prominent shopping district in Lucknow, likened to Chowringhee in Calcutta.

Chowringhee.description: A famous commercial area in Calcutta, used as a reference point for Hazratganj.

Malkani & Co..description: An antique and curio shop in Hazratganj, run by Mr Malkani.

Murshidabad.description: A city in West Bengal, famous for its ivory and antique crafts.

Badshah Nagar.description: A locality in Lucknow where Mr Sarkar resides.

The Empire Book Stall.description: A bookshop in Hazratganj, visited by Feluda and Topshe.

Neville Cardus.description: A renowned English cricket writer, whose books are sought after by Feluda.

Bradman.description: Refers to Sir Donald Bradman, legendary Australian cricketer, whose autobiography is mentioned.

Ranji.description: Refers to K.S. Ranjitsinhji, a famous Indian cricketer from the early 20th century.

Kwality restaurant.description: A well-known restaurant in Hazratganj, where the characters meet for tea.

Howrah.description: A city adjacent to Kolkata, known for its railway station, mentioned as Ganesh Guha's destination.

Military Academy.description: Refers to an institution for military training, attended by Mahabir.

attardaan.description: A container used for storing attar, a traditional Indian perfume.

hubble-bubble.description: A traditional Indian water pipe, also known as a hookah.

Ambika.description: An old classmate of Dhiru Kaka who became a sannyasi and is seen being revered by followers at the station.

Hrishikesh.description: Also spelled Rishikesh, a town in northern India known for its spiritual significance and as a gateway to the Himalayas.

Bareilly.description: A city in northern India, mentioned as a stop on the train journey.

Hardoi.description: A town in Uttar Pradesh, India, where the train halts during the journey.

Swami.description: A Hindu religious title for a monk or spiritual teacher.

chaiwalla.description: A vendor who sells tea, commonly found at Indian railway stations.

Gitanjali.description: A famous collection of poems by Rabindranath Tagore, originally written in Bengali.

Urdu.description: A language spoken in South Asia, especially in India and Pakistan, associated with poetry and music.

Wajid Ali Shah.description: The last Nawab of Awadh, known for his patronage of the arts and music.

Matiaburuz.description: A locality in Kolkata (Calcutta), historically home to Muslim tailors.

Rajen Mullik.description: A wealthy historical figure mentioned as a collaborator in founding Calcutta's first zoo.

Ganges.description: A sacred river in India, central to Hindu religious practices.

thumri.description: A genre of semi-classical Indian music, known for its romantic or devotional themes.

Bilash Babu.description: A Bengali gentleman from Allahabad, introduced as a palmist who reads Bonobihari Babu’s hand.

Sheetal Das.description: The owner or manager of the dharamshala where the group stays.

dharamshala.description: A dharamshala is a rest house or inn, often for pilgrims, providing basic accommodation. In the story, Sheetal Das’s dharamshala is the specific rest house where the group stays in Haridwar.

Baba Daksheshwar.description: A temple in Haridwar, dedicated to a Hindu deity, visited by pilgrims.

Vaishnav.description: A devotee of Lord Vishnu, often associated with specific religious practices.

panda.description: A Hindu priest or guide in pilgrimage centers who assists visitors with rituals and records family histories.

coolie.description: A manual laborer or porter, especially at railway stations in India.

angeethees.description: Portable clay or metal stoves used for heating or cooking, especially in North India.

bhajan.description: A devotional song, typically sung in praise of Hindu deities.

raga.description: A melodic framework in Indian classical music, associated with specific moods and times of day.

dhoti.description: A traditional Indian garment, a rectangular piece of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs.

kurta.description: A loose, collarless shirt worn in South Asia, often paired with a dhoti or pajama.

shikari.description: A hunter, especially one who hunts wild animals in India.

hydrophobia.description: Another term for rabies, a viral disease that can be transmitted by animal bites.

Chevrolet.description: An American automobile brand; here, it refers to an old-fashioned taxi.

puri-subzi.description: A popular Indian breakfast dish consisting of deep-fried bread (puri) served with a spiced vegetable curry (subzi).

woollens.description: Warm clothing made of wool, commonly worn in colder regions of India.

Pandeyji.description: A sadhu (holy man) who is said to live alone in the jungle and keep a python.

Jim Corbett.description: A renowned British-Indian hunter, tracker, and conservationist famous for hunting man-eating tigers and leopards in India.

Howrah Bridge.description: An iconic cantilever bridge over the Hooghly River in West Bengal, connecting Kolkata and Howrah.

Jab chhor chaley Lucknow nagari Kahen ha.description: A line from an Urdu song, expressing the sorrow of leaving Lucknow.

Naulakha Company.description: A reputed jewelry company in Calcutta from which the ring was purchased.

Black Widow.description: The Black Widow is a highly venomous spider native to Africa, used by a character to intimidate another. It is also referred to as the African spider, a dangerous species used as a plot device.

Emperor’s ring.description: A valuable and central object in the story, believed to have imperial significance.

durrie.description: A traditional Indian cotton rug or mat, often used for sitting or sleeping.
